title: Teaching workspace sidebar research
method: Team review of distinct substantive public pages, with source-specific notes. Counts exclude search snippets, mirrors, repeated views, inaccessible pages and navigation-only indexes. The count is pages, not websites or independent studies.
scope: Research and local read-only source inspection. No application changes or tutor usability experiment in this review.

pages.title: Build Responsive Real-World Websites with HTML and CSS
pages.keyFinding: The public curriculum covers typography, limited color palettes, whitespace, hierarchy, familiar patterns, accordions, carousels, and application layouts. Teaching a component does not establish that it fits every task.
pages.application: Use consistent spacing, typography, icons, and emphasis; select workspace components by teaching tasks.
pages.evidenceType: Public course curriculum and descriptions; paid lectures not viewed

pages.title: Web Design for Web Developers: Build Beautiful Websites
pages.keyFinding: The public course describes one base color with tints, readable typography, whitespace, hierarchy, and alignment of user goals with the product. Its conversion advice serves marketing tasks.
pages.application: Use purple selectively and group related controls; do not carry marketing urgency or repeated calls to action into a live lesson.
pages.evidenceType: Public course curriculum and descriptions; lectures not viewed

pages.title: Tabs, Used Right
pages.keyFinding: Tabs work for a few clearly labeled content groups when users do not need to compare the groups simultaneously. Overflow reduces discoverability; the default panel gets disproportionate attention.
pages.application: Keep material categories visible; keep active call controls outside material tabs; avoid nested Materials/Games then material tabs.

pages.title: Accordions Are Not Always the Answer for Complex Content on Desktops
pages.keyFinding: Accordions reduce visible length but add decisions and clicks and can hide needed content. They fit selective access better than content users must routinely open together.
pages.application: Do not accordion every teaching tool or hide the whole Materials workspace.

pages.title: Progressive Disclosure
pages.keyFinding: Keep frequently needed options on the primary view and disclose advanced or rare options on request. Clear labels and shallow levels are essential.
pages.application: Expose Add face, upload, letter entry, sound-box count and current game level; disclose device selection and uncommon settings.

pages.title: Accordion Icons: Which Signifiers Work Best
pages.keyFinding: The study found a downward caret more clearly signaled expansion in place than alternatives. The experiment placed icons to the right of labels; results do not automatically generalize to other positions.
pages.application: Use a labeled expansion row with a chevron and a state change for optional settings.

pages.title: Carousel Usability: Designing an Effective UI for Websites with Content Overload
pages.keyFinding: Users can overlook frames beyond the first. The article addresses promotional/content carousels and emphasizes navigation and alternatives, rather than claiming every sequence should be removed.
pages.application: Do not carousel teaching categories or the full image library; intentional lesson-page navigation is a separate task.

pages.title: Does Your Form Really Need a Dropdown List
pages.keyFinding: Dropdown selects save space but hide options and add interaction cost. Selection inputs are distinct from command menus and navigation. Defaults can obscure alternatives.
pages.application: Use visible controls for a short, frequent sound-box count or level selection; reserve selects for longer collection/device choices.

pages.title: Dropdowns: Design Guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Command menus, navigation menus and attribute selectors serve different goals. Long menus and interdependent changing options create steering and consistency problems.
pages.application: Use explicit verbs for actions, stable category labels, and avoid making basic tools dependent on opening another menu.

pages.title: 8 Design Guidelines for Complex Applications
pages.keyFinding: Complex applications should preserve capability while reducing clutter, support fluid task sequences, coordinate tool transitions, and allow secondary information without leaving the primary environment.
pages.application: Keep board, active video and current materials accessible together; preserve browsing state; put game adjustments inline.

pages.title: Memory Recognition and Recall in User Interfaces
pages.keyFinding: Recognition benefits from contextual cues and is generally easier than recalling an item from scratch. Interfaces can reduce memory demands by exposing relevant choices and context.
pages.application: Use actual card thumbnails and clear labels; restore selection, search and scroll so tutors can resume.

pages.title: Modal and Nonmodal Dialogs: When and When Not to Use Them
pages.keyFinding: Modal dialogs block the background and interrupt workflow. They can fit focused, relevant tasks but are inappropriate when users need to consult or interact with background content.
pages.application: Keep routine game adjustments in a nonmodal panel; retain a deliberate larger picture editor with visible completion and exit controls.

pages.title: Carousels on Mobile Devices
pages.keyFinding: Sequential access and weak discoverability make long carousels inefficient. For large collections, the article recommends a list with direct access.
pages.application: Use a searchable thumbnail grid for 28 cards, with no required sideways swiping through each item.

pages.title: Designing Effective Contextual Menus: 10 Guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Contextual menus reduce clutter but have weak clues about their contents. Keep essential frequent actions visible and place secondary actions close to their affected object.
pages.application: Keep Add face and call controls visible; use object-specific Duplicate/Delete and uncommon card actions close to their item.

pages.title: Accordions vs Tabs: What We Learned
pages.keyFinding: Its small content-page tests found no clear desktop winner and mobile problems when users could not see content change. The authors favor editing excess content and validating behavior, not declaring a universal component winner.
pages.application: Make panel changes immediately visible in the short sidebar; test realistic tasks instead of relying on preference votes.
pages.evidenceType: First-party usability report; small samples and content-page context

pages.title: Avoid Using Horizontal Tabs for Main Product Page Sections
pages.keyFinding: In ecommerce product-page tests, shoppers often expected vertical scrolling and missed content in horizontal tabs. This concerns product information discovery rather than repeated use of application tools.
pages.application: Do not infer that all tabs are bad; retain short, stable material tabs but ensure discoverability and task-test them.
pages.evidenceType: Ecommerce research; indirect relevance to teaching workspace

pages.title: Toolbars
pages.keyFinding: Miro documents separate board, creation, collaboration and canvas-navigation regions, with core tools accessible and some secondary integrations behind tools menus.
pages.application: Separate direct board tools from materials, collaboration and zoom. Adopt task grouping without copying Miro's full complexity.
pages.evidenceType: Product documentation; precedent, not comparative usability evidence

pages.title: Explore FigJam Files
pages.keyFinding: FigJam documents distinct board, panels and tool regions; the toolbar separates navigation, objects, tools and inserts. Different tasks have recognizable locations.
pages.application: Give materials a stable home; keep left board tools and bottom zoom separate; avoid moving categories during a lesson.
pages.evidenceType: Product documentation; precedent, not proof of best design

pages.title: Whiteboard Tools and Features
pages.keyFinding: Lessonspace documents direct library/upload access, object-specific actions, zoom and permissions. Its tool inventory illustrates how resource insertion differs from object editing and viewport control.
pages.application: Keep material insertion, contextual object editing and viewport controls in their own consistent regions.
pages.evidenceType: Product documentation; no independent comparative test

pages.title: A Quick Start Guide to Explain Everything Whiteboard
pages.keyFinding: The native-app guide separates creation tools, zoom/pan, recording and slide sorting. Some controls appear only after their task starts, such as timeline controls after recording.
pages.application: Use task relevance for secondary controls and reserve a separate location for future lesson pages; do not copy native layout literally into the web sidebar.
pages.evidenceType: Native-app product documentation; indirect web precedent

pages.title: Accordion
pages.keyFinding: Accordions support selective access to related sections and can suit repeat users, but hide content and require user evidence. Tabs better support quick switching; accordions support simultaneous sections. Do not nest accordion, tabs, or details components.
pages.application: Consider a few optional independent settings sections; avoid an accordion inside every materials tab and keep essential teaching controls visible.

pages.title: Tabs
pages.keyFinding: Tabs can help regular users switch quickly between clearly labelled related sections when simultaneous viewing is unnecessary. They are unsuitable for sequential reading or comparison across panels and should not replace page navigation.
pages.application: A small Letters, Pictures, Worksheets switcher fits the fast category-switching case; preserve each panel's task state as an app-specific implementation hypothesis.

pages.title: Details
pages.keyFinding: Details reveals information needed by only some users. It is less prominent than tabs or an accordion and suits a single short, less important section. Information most users need must remain visible.
pages.application: Hide optional upload explanations or advanced help, rather than hiding Open picture library or the main Add action.

pages.title: Select
pages.keyFinding: Select is a last resort for public-facing services because some users struggle with it. Reduce options before choosing a select. Settings may have a sensible default, while questions should not be preselected.
pages.application: Use visible options for a few primary tool categories; reserve a labelled select for a longer collection or ordering choice if research supports it.

pages.title: Button
pages.keyFinding: Button text should describe the action in sentence case. The default button identifies the main action; several competing main actions reduce impact and make the next step harder to identify.
pages.application: Make Add face or Add to board primary within a material context; give secondary operations quieter treatment.

pages.title: Summary list
pages.keyFinding: Summary lists present key-value facts, not arbitrary task lists or tabular data. Related row actions need context, including accessible labels identifying the affected fact. Headings or summary cards can structure multiple lists.
pages.application: Use compact labelled facts for room or material metadata rather than giving every fact its own prominent control or generic card.

pages.title: Accordion
pages.keyFinding: Accordions suit limited space when users need only selected pieces. They increase decision and interaction costs when unnecessary. Make the entire header selectable and separate inner interactive controls enough to prevent accidental collapse.
pages.application: If optional settings collapse, give each header a large target and keep its buttons away from the collapse trigger.

pages.title: Button
pages.keyFinding: Give the important action a distinctive style, avoid too many buttons, and use short verb-led labels. Explain why unavailable actions are unavailable. Native buttons and visible focus states preserve expected keyboard behavior.
pages.application: Reduce repeated purple buttons in the sidebar and show clear readiness or permission explanations for disabled teaching actions.

pages.title: Card
pages.keyFinding: Cards group related modular content, not every bordered section. Repeated images and redundant content make cards harder to distinguish. Keep imagery responsive, styling simple, and headings in a logical hierarchy.
pages.application: Use distinct real thumbnails and concise titles in the picture library; avoid extra repeated metadata and decorative nested card containers.

pages.title: Combo box
pages.keyFinding: The guidance considers combo boxes for more than fifteen choices and limited space, but warns about known assistive-technology usability issues and currently suggests considering select instead. Options need familiar language and a persistent label.
pages.application: Do not introduce a custom searchable dropdown casually; prefer straightforward library search and evaluate assistive-technology support before any combobox.

pages.title: Side navigation
pages.keyFinding: Side navigation represents a shallow navigational hierarchy. Existing horizontal and vertical navigation may need simplification. Show the current location, keep labels short, and test whether long or deep structures hide destinations.
pages.application: Avoid duplicating Games or Pictures in several competing sidebar and toolbar locations without a clear role for each.

pages.title: Search
pages.keyFinding: Search should retain the submitted terms, allow enough input width to inspect the query, and keep simple searching as the default. Advanced search increases mistakes for users who need only one or two terms.
pages.application: Keep a compact labelled material search available and retain its query after opening a card; make extra filtering optional.

pages.title: Select
pages.keyFinding: Use select sparingly for roughly seven to fifteen options under space constraints. Fewer choices favor radios, navigation needs navigation controls, and multi-select needs checkboxes. Do not automatically submit when a choice changes.
pages.application: Three main teaching categories should stay directly visible rather than becoming a select; longer filter choices can use a labelled native control.

pages.title: Modal
pages.keyFinding: Modals interrupt the main workflow and should be a last resort. Users should trigger them. Use clear actions, size content to avoid unnecessary scrolling, and avoid complicated flows or many nested interactive components.
pages.application: Use a large picture inspection surface only when needed; do not make routine tool switching or every successful add require a modal.

pages.title: Button group
pages.keyFinding: Group actions only when they share context, avoid mixing destructive and ordinary commands, and limit choices. Segmented groups suit related views, but more than three choices may fail on small screens; communicate the current state.
pages.application: Use a compact related-view switcher for three material types and separate Clear board from everyday editing commands.

pages.title: Tooltip
pages.keyFinding: Tooltips suit brief noncritical help and should be a last resort for constrained space. They must not contain essential task information, block content, or conflict with other hover and focus behavior.
pages.application: Keep visible short tool labels; use optional tooltips for clarification rather than as the only explanation of a teaching control.

pages.title: Details
pages.keyFinding: Details suits information only some users need and is less prominent than an expander. NHS reports some form users hesitate to open link-styled details because they fear navigation will lose their progress.
pages.application: Use clear expand wording and a recognisable disclosure affordance for optional instructions; retain user work when opening or closing it.

pages.title: Expander
pages.keyFinding: Expanders can break overwhelming information into manageable portions when users need them. Test simpler structure first. NHS advises against expanders on pages containing other interactive elements because they can distract users.
pages.application: Treat a stack of expanding live tool panels cautiously; the whiteboard is interaction-heavy, unlike the informational pages used in NHS research.

pages.title: Card
pages.keyFinding: Cards visually group related content and actions. Keep them short for scanning. Both clickable and non-clickable forms exist; avoid wrapping a complete clickable card in an anchor because of screen-reader difficulties.
pages.application: Give each picture a concise thumbnail card with explicit actions; avoid a giant nested interactive link around crop and add buttons.

pages.title: Select
pages.keyFinding: NHS calls select a last resort because some users find it difficult. Narrow the options or use radios when possible. A select does not support accessible multiple selection; use another method such as checkboxes.
pages.application: Keep main teaching choices visible and use clear optional filter controls; avoid converting all sidebar choices into dropdowns.

pages.title: Buttons
pages.keyFinding: Buttons carry out actions rather than ordinary navigation. Avoid excessive buttons. On smaller screens, full-width buttons are easier to press; do not shrink button height below the system's supported smaller size.
pages.application: Reduce button count while preserving comfortable mobile touch targets; make the immediate add action clear rather than tiny.

pages.title: Accordion
pages.keyFinding: Accordions hide information and increase interaction cost. Use clear headings, avoid nesting and empty sections, and review performance. Frequent use of Open all may indicate that users cannot find the information they need.
pages.application: Use observed tutor behavior to validate collapsible settings; if teachers reopen everything, simplify the panel rather than adding more disclosure.

pages.title: Tabs
pages.pattern: Stable view switching and label fit
pages.keyFinding: Tabs keep switching controls in place and suit one section at a time. Order by need, label succinctly, avoid disabled or wrapping tabs, and remember that content taller than the viewport makes switching harder.
pages.application: Keep category controls accessible while the material list scrolls, and use short labels that remain on one row at supported widths.

pages.title: Details
pages.keyFinding: Use details when only some users need one section of information. It shortens pages but must not hide content most users require. Short descriptive trigger text helps users decide whether to expand it.
pages.application: A single Advanced options or Help disclosure can be more appropriate than creating an accordion for one setting.

pages.title: Select (dropdown)
pages.keyFinding: Select handles one choice from a long list, with usability and accessibility drawbacks. Short lists favor radios and multiple choices favor checkboxes. Include a label and use alphabetical ordering unless another ordering better serves users.
pages.application: Use labelled collection filtering only where the option list warrants it; keep frequent material destinations directly available.

pages.title: Side navigation
pages.keyFinding: Side navigation shows distinct destinations and the current location. Keep nested structures below ten sections and three levels, avoid duplication, and keep link labels short. Its mobile form becomes an expandable list.
pages.application: Avoid layering a category bar, another navigation stack, and duplicate tool shortcuts without clear distinctions.

pages.title: Error message
pages.keyFinding: Validation errors belong next to the affected field and in a summary. Preserve entered values and use clear corrective language. Permission or service failures are different problems and should not be presented as user input mistakes.
pages.application: Distinguish an invalid file from a disconnected lesson or denied action; show a specific recovery path without deleting the tutor's inputs.

pages.title: Error summary
pages.pattern: Find and recover from form errors
pages.keyFinding: When form validation fails, an error summary should receive focus, link to affected inputs, and repeat the corresponding inline error wording. Each link should lead to the field that needs correction.
pages.application: For multi-field upload or worksheet setup, make failures discoverable and link to the correction rather than leaving errors below the visible panel.

pages.title: Structuring forms
pages.keyFinding: Start by asking only necessary questions and prioritising common scenarios. One thing per page supports unfamiliar tasks; research may justify combining content for repeat-use internal services that require fast task switching.
pages.application: Do not transplant a one-question-per-page rule literally into a live teaching workspace; evaluate tutor frequency and switching needs.

pages.title: Site search
pages.keyFinding: Users can submit search with Return or the magnifying-glass control. A search landmark, input label, and accessible button name communicate the function to screen-reader users even when the visible label is omitted.
pages.application: Ensure sidebar material search works from the keyboard and has a meaningful accessible name, without adding an oversized explanatory header.

pages.title: Making your service look like GOV.UK
pages.keyFinding: Patterns may be adapted or replaced when research shows user needs are unmet. Non-government products may use patterns but should retain their own identity, and admin-style interfaces may require different patterns.
pages.application: Borrow interaction principles without copying government branding or treating public form guidance as an exact sidebar template.

pages.title: Search filters
pages.pattern: Optional filters and visible applied state
pages.keyFinding: Filters need useful metadata and clear categories. Mobile filters collapse above results and require Apply. Show removable applied-filter tags and Clear all. Reported filter use is low and more common among topic experts.
pages.application: Let tutors reveal optional library filters, show active filters compactly, and restore the complete library with one clear action.

pages.title: Tabs
pages.keyFinding: Tabs organize distinct but related content within one context, including side panels. They are unsuitable for comparing simultaneously needed information or filtering the same content; those tasks need different arrangements.
pages.application: Use stable Letters, Pictures, and Worksheets categories rather than mixing category switching with board actions.

pages.title: Accordion
pages.keyFinding: Accordions save scarce space and reduce scrolling when users do not need every section. They hide content and add interaction cost, so they are unsuitable when the whole content must be read.
pages.application: Collapse optional configuration, not the material currently being taught or the primary add action.

pages.title: Content switcher
pages.keyFinding: Content switchers change alternate views or subsets of related content in the same area. Distinct categories belong in tabs, while binary settings should use toggles rather than a content switcher.
pages.application: Reserve a compact switcher for grid/list or content subsets; avoid another tab-like navigation layer.

pages.title: Search
pages.keyFinding: Search can operate globally, per page, or within a component. It helps with large or complex sets, but is unnecessary when a small collection is already easy to find in one view.
pages.application: Keep picture search scoped to the current material collection and avoid empty search chrome for tiny tool groups.

pages.title: Dropdown
pages.keyFinding: Dropdowns support filtering, sorting, and choosing options; they should remain straightforward rather than nested or complex. Native selects deserve consideration in form-heavy or frequently mobile experiences.
pages.application: Use a labeled collection filter rather than putting teaching cards or nested tool interfaces inside a dropdown.

pages.title: Contained list
pages.keyFinding: Contained lists organize consistently structured rows in cards, sidebars, and disclosure surfaces. They can support inline actions and interactivity, but should not become deeply nested or substitute for multi-column data structures.
pages.application: Use compact rows for saved materials or games instead of many individually padded cards.

pages.title: Select
pages.keyFinding: Selects work best for single-option form submission and inherit browser rendering. Carbon distinguishes them from dropdowns used for actions, filtering, or sorting, and discourages selects for fewer than three choices.
pages.application: Keep small teaching-mode choices visible; use native select for appropriate mobile configuration fields.

pages.title: Menu
pages.keyFinding: Menus disclose actions relevant to a selected element or interface area. They are useful for less frequent or advanced commands; complex inputs belong in a popover rather than being forced into menu items.
pages.application: Place infrequent commands in an overflow menu while keeping Add face and the current game controls directly available.

pages.title: Tile
pages.keyFinding: Tiles group related information or actions in flexible containers and support clickable or selectable variants. Cards build on that foundation with richer hierarchy and multiple actions; container choice should match intended interaction.
pages.application: Avoid making every sidebar section a large elevated card when a compact grouped surface suffices.

pages.title: Modal
pages.keyFinding: Modals interrupt the underlying workflow and should serve short, infrequent tasks. Carbon recommends moving repeatedly performed tasks onto the main page rather than requiring a modal every time.
pages.application: Keep repeated material selection/addition available inline; reserve a larger focused dialog for detailed crop or library browsing.

pages.title: Tooltip
pages.keyFinding: Tooltips provide contextual, nonessential help on hover or focus, including names for unlabeled controls. They should be used when useful rather than duplicating tooltips already supplied by components.
pages.application: Do not rely on hover help to teach children or touch users how to find essential controls.

pages.title: React Accordion
pages.keyFinding: Accordion headers summarize related sections and use consistent chevrons. Required information should not be hidden inside accordions; multiple sections may remain open where this helps without overwhelming the experience.
pages.application: Use Video and Games disclosure cautiously, with the active teaching controls kept visible and clear state in each header.

pages.title: React Drawer
pages.keyFinding: Inline drawers support simultaneous interaction with main content; overlay drawers block or obscure it. Headers, bodies, and optional footers establish structure, with sticky controls useful unless small viewports or high zoom require more content space.
pages.application: Keep desktop materials alongside the board and use a deliberate compact-screen drawer rather than shrinking both until unusable.

pages.title: React Toolbar
pages.keyFinding: Toolbars expose frequent task actions, organize related commands with spacing or dividers, and separate destructive commands. Overflow should carry text labels, and familiar icon buttons still require accessible labels and explanatory tooltips.
pages.application: Retain a compact board tool rail and separate Clear board; move selection-specific picture actions near the selected object.

pages.title: React Tablist
pages.keyFinding: Tablists divide related content without separate pages and reduce scrolling. Horizontal tabs should not wrap; when narrow space pushes too many into overflow, an accordion or dropdown may be more usable.
pages.application: Use concise parallel material names and test the real narrow panel width before adding more category tabs.

pages.title: React Dropdown
pages.keyFinding: Dropdown placeholders supplement rather than replace labels. Single selections close the menu; multiple selections remain open until dismissal. Native selects offer advantages for mobile forms, and inline popups improve VoiceOver navigation.
pages.application: Give collection filters persistent labels and expose the chosen collection without opening the control.

pages.title: React Menu
pages.keyFinding: Menus usually invoke actions or change context, unlike data-entry controls. Related options should be grouped, frequent actions ordered first, dangerous ones last, and excessive submenu nesting avoided.
pages.application: Use overflow for Duplicate, Download, or advanced settings; do not hide the core teaching workflow in nested menus.

pages.title: React Carousel
pages.keyFinding: Carousels cycle through content independently of the surrounding page and can use steps or image thumbnails. Autoplay must be pausable, and responsive content must preserve image proportions and support substantial zoom.
pages.application: A manually controlled recent-material strip is plausible; a carousel should not become the only route to essential tools.

pages.title: Searchbox
pages.keyFinding: A consistent search layout supports learned behavior, with clear controls appearing only when text exists. On small viewports search may expand from an icon, and ordering should prioritize the most relevant results.
pages.application: Keep one scoped search per material category and retain the query when tutors switch away and return.

pages.title: React Popover
pages.keyFinding: Popovers suit brief nonessential contextual information and interactive content, but should not cover important material needed simultaneously. Avoid nesting them; essential or substantial content belongs on the page or a panel.
pages.application: Use a small anchored panel for optional settings, not a multi-step material browser layered over the whiteboard.

pages.title: React Select
pages.keyFinding: Native selects support single choices from a list and are suited to form submission and mobile usability. Labels should be descriptive, options parallel, and a meaningful default selection visible from first render.
pages.application: Use a select for longer settings lists, with clear defaults; keep a short set of core material categories visible.

pages.title: React Combobox
pages.keyFinding: Comboboxes filter long option sets as people type and can optionally accept free-form values. Selection should remain apparent without reopening the menu, while labeling and keyboard behavior need explicit consideration.
pages.application: Consider searchable collections only if the library grows substantially; avoid complex autocomplete for a tiny fixed set.

pages.title: React Card
pages.keyFinding: Cards represent one concept or object with concise, action-oriented content. A whole-card click suits one obvious action; multiple actions need explicit controls, deliberate hierarchy, and predictable keyboard focus behavior.
pages.application: Use consistent teaching-card thumbnails, one dominant Add face action, and a compact secondary menu instead of three tall button rows.

pages.title: Accordion usage guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Accordions help reveal related information as needed in limited space, but overuse adds clicks when people need all content. More complex or deeply nested information may need tabs or a tree instead.
pages.application: An accordion is useful for optional settings, not as the entire materials information architecture.

pages.title: Tabs usage guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Tabs should represent equal-importance peer content. Avoid multiple nested tab levels, inconsistent icon treatment, and truncating several labels merely to fit; scrolling or a picker are possible overflow strategies.
pages.application: Keep one clear materials category level and use another component for filters or options within that category.

pages.title: App frame
pages.keyFinding: Spectrum separates navigation, global actions, and transient contextual actions. It distinguishes browsing from editing, where canvas content is the focus, and frames predictable structure as adaptable rather than prescribing every product-specific placement.
pages.application: Keep the board visually dominant; separate material browsing from selected-object commands and room-level session controls.

pages.title: ActionBar
pages.keyFinding: Action bars support actions on one or more selected items and can report the selection count. Their documented behavior hides the bar at zero selected items, connecting command visibility to selection context.
pages.application: Show Crop, Duplicate, and Delete only for the relevant board selection rather than occupying permanent sidebar space.

pages.title: ContextualHelp
pages.keyFinding: Contextual help supplies extra information about an adjacent component or an overall view. Its popover supports a heading, explanatory content, and optional links, with placement tied to the triggering control.
pages.application: Move lengthy optional instructions into nearby help while retaining short essential labels directly on teaching controls.

pages.title: Drawer design guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Drawers can overlay content or sit beside it; inline drawers keep primary content visible while making it more compact. A splitter is appropriate when users need to adjust panel space, not when default sizing already suffices.
pages.application: Consider a bounded resizable desktop materials panel, keeping the whiteboard present and enforcing a usable minimum canvas width.

pages.title: Accordion design guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Accordions provide structure when space is limited but have a high interaction cost, so PatternFly recommends sparing use. Their best fit is optional simple sections rather than complex deeply nested information.
pages.application: Avoid forcing repeated expand/collapse hunting during a live lesson; keep the current tool and its controls easy to reach.

pages.title: Tabs design guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Tabs group related page subviews and should remain few for a better experience. The guidance covers overflow and visually differentiated hierarchy, with component-contained tabs styled less prominently than full-page primary navigation.
pages.application: Use compact secondary tabs inside Materials rather than large competing navigation cards.

pages.title: Toolbar design guidelines
pages.keyFinding: Toolbars should sit near the data they control, group related filters, and keep only the most important actions exposed. On smaller screens filter groups can collapse into a dedicated panel while counts remain informative.
pages.application: Place scoped search and a compact filter trigger directly above material results, showing the result count and active filters.

pages.title: Accordion Pattern
pages.keyFinding: Accordions reduce scrolling through vertically grouped sections while keeping section headings visible. Header buttons communicate expanded state; controls and reading order remain available to keyboard users.
pages.application: Use a few named tutor sections, with state visible in their headers; avoid nested accordions and excessive region landmarks.

pages.title: Tabs Pattern
pages.keyFinding: Tabs expose peer content categories while displaying one panel. Automatic activation is appropriate only when panels appear without noticeable delay; otherwise explicit activation prevents slow keyboard navigation.
pages.application: Keep Letters, Pictures and Worksheets visible as stable material categories. Preserve state and preload or use manual activation.

pages.title: Carousel Pattern
pages.keyFinding: Sequential slides need previous/next controls and clear slide identity. Automatic rotation must stop on focus or hover and require explicit restart; individually tabbable slide selectors add keyboard effort.
pages.application: Do not make a rotating carousel the primary tool navigation. If a card deck is sequential, provide manual controls and position labels.

pages.title: Disclosure Pattern
pages.keyFinding: A disclosure consists of a button and its controlled content, with Enter/Space operation and expanded state. Directional indicators conventionally communicate whether more content is hidden or shown.
pages.application: Collapse optional search filters or video settings behind a labeled button and chevron; leave the primary material action visible.

pages.title: Menu Button Pattern
pages.keyFinding: Menu buttons open command lists and move keyboard focus into the menu. A downward indicator and expanded state reveal availability; menus require their own complete keyboard interaction.
pages.application: Reserve an overflow command menu for infrequent actions, not the main Materials categories or fields containing persistent selected values.

pages.title: Combobox Pattern
pages.keyFinding: Comboboxes represent a selected value and may filter suggestions through typing. Menu buttons have no value; editable fields should retain native text-editing behavior and offer predictable cancellation.
pages.application: Use a labeled native select for a small collection filter; consider a searchable combobox only when its option count warrants the added interaction complexity.

pages.title: Dialog (Modal) Pattern
pages.keyFinding: Modal dialogs make the surrounding application inert, contain keyboard focus, support Escape, and normally return focus to their trigger. Initial focus depends on content size and task risk.
pages.application: Use a focused dialog for large picture browsing or cropping, with visible Close and a persistent primary action; use nonmodal controls for frequent board work.

pages.title: Toolbar Pattern
pages.keyFinding: A toolbar groups at least three controls and can reduce tab stops by using one entry point with arrow navigation. Its orientation and accessible name communicate the control grouping.
pages.application: Keep common Select/Draw/Erase actions together, separate destructive Clear, and do not mix text-input arrow handling with toolbar navigation.

pages.title: Accordion Example
pages.keyFinding: The example uses heading-contained buttons, controlled panel IDs, and expanded state. APG stresses that examples require assistive-technology testing, especially on mobile, before production use.
pages.application: Implement section headings with native buttons and validate actual screen reader/touch behavior rather than copying illustrative markup untested.

pages.title: Tabs with Manual Activation Example
pages.keyFinding: Manual tabs separate focusing a tab from displaying its panel. The example separately marks selection and focus and allows layouts to reflow when magnified.
pages.application: Keep the selected material tab visibly distinct from keyboard focus; avoid firing slow material changes merely because a tutor arrows across labels.

pages.title: Disclosure Navigation Menu Example
pages.keyFinding: Ordinary navigation dropdowns can use disclosure semantics rather than ARIA menu roles. Escape closes an open dropdown and returns focus; visible carets must survive high-contrast settings.
pages.application: A plain expandable filters or settings group should remain a disclosure, without imposing command-menu keyboard behavior on everyday links and fields.

pages.title: Select-Only Combobox Example
pages.keyFinding: Exploring options need not commit a new value. Escape preserves the current choice, and the active option must be scrolled into view because accessibility focus alone does not do that.
pages.application: A custom collection selector must support cancellation, type-ahead and visible active options under zoom; prefer native select unless custom behavior is necessary.

pages.title: Developing a Keyboard Interface
pages.keyFinding: ARIA does not supply keyboard behavior automatically. Familiar Tab-between/arrow-within conventions, persistent visible focus, and explicit recovery after hiding or deleting the focused element make navigation predictable.
pages.application: When collapsing a sidebar section or closing a picker, deliberately restore focus; distinguish selected board object, selected tab, and current keyboard target.

pages.title: Understanding Target Size (Minimum)
pages.keyFinding: WCAG 2.2 AA generally requires targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with defined exceptions including spacing. Larger targets improve operation even where minimal spacing technically conforms.
pages.application: Size chevrons, Close, Add face, and sound-box controls generously; do not equate a compliant minimum with an ideal child-friendly target.

pages.title: Understanding Dragging Movements
pages.keyFinding: Dragging functionality needs a single-pointer alternative without dragging, unless essential. Keyboard equivalence alone is insufficient because touch users may not have a physical keyboard.
pages.application: Keep Add face/Add to board buttons and click-select/click-place or move controls alongside optional dragging. Do not require holding a modifier to complete essential tasks.

pages.title: Understanding Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
pages.keyFinding: Keyboard-focused controls must not be entirely hidden by author-created content. Sticky headers, footers and persistent nonmodal panels are common causes; complete visibility remains the stronger design objective.
pages.application: A sticky picker footer must reserve content space, and scrolling a sidebar must reveal its focused controls above any fixed action row.

pages.title: Understanding Consistent Help
pages.keyFinding: Repeated help mechanisms across a page set must retain their relative order unless users initiate a qualifying layout change. Consistency helps people find support without relearning its location.
pages.application: Keep lesson Help/connection troubleshooting in a stable place across tutor tools; contextual instructions can still appear beside the relevant action.

pages.title: Understanding Status Messages
pages.keyFinding: Success, waiting, progress and error messages should be programmatically announced without taking focus. Status feedback is intended to inform users while avoiding unnecessary interruption of their current work.
pages.application: Announce picture upload progress, added-to-board confirmation and reconnect state politely; do not open dialogs or move focus for routine success.

pages.title: Understanding Animation from Interactions
pages.keyFinding: Nonessential interaction-triggered motion can be disabled under WCAG AAA. Respecting reduced-motion preferences or removing unnecessary animation supports users with vestibular symptoms and distraction.
pages.application: Use restrained disclosure/drawer transitions and honor prefers-reduced-motion. Avoid animated tool rearrangement, parallax, and autoplay in a live lesson workspace.

pages.title: Understanding On Focus
pages.keyFinding: Receiving focus must not trigger a change of context. Expanding local content is not automatically a context change, but opening a window or moving focus unexpectedly can disorient users.
pages.application: Do not open the full material library or move to a new board merely because a field or tab receives focus; require intentional activation.

pages.title: Understanding On Input
pages.keyFinding: Changing a control's value must not unexpectedly change context without advance notice. Updating part of a form can remain in context when its overall structure and focus are preserved.
pages.application: Collection filtering can update visible results in place, but choosing an option should not unexpectedly launch a game, close the panel, or navigate away.

pages.title: Understanding Consistent Navigation
pages.keyFinding: Repeated navigation retains relative order across a page set unless users initiate a change. Consistent layout supports spatial memory, magnification and sequential screen-reader navigation.
pages.application: Keep Materials category positions predictable; put an active game's controls in a stable active area rather than unexpectedly shuffling the main navigation.

pages.title: Understanding Focus Order
pages.keyFinding: Sequential focus order must preserve meaning and operation. Matching the visual reading order is usually helpful, and opening or closing dialogs requires logical focus transitions.
pages.application: Make keyboard progression follow section header, search/filter, material cards and actions. Avoid visually moving a panel without considering its DOM and focus order.

pages.title: Making Content Usable for People with Cognitive and Learning Disabilities
pages.publisher: W3C Cognitive and Learning Disabilities Accessibility Task Force
pages.keyFinding: The guide recommends short required workflows, controllable interruptions, clear orientation cues and limited primary choices. Optional steps should not obstruct important tasks; simplification must retain sufficient instructions and recovery cues.
pages.application: Keep Add face direct; make cropping optional. Remember tutor context when switching panels, show current activity, and reduce student-facing choices without hiding essential instructions.

pages.title: Organize Information and Resources, Consideration 6.3
pages.keyFinding: When maintaining information in working memory is not the learning objective, organizational scaffolds can help keep it available. CAST suggests organizers, categorization prompts, checklists and note-taking guides.
pages.application: A prepared or recent-materials area and retained search context can reduce material hunting during teaching; validate that these aids support rather than crowd the board.

pages.title: Address Biases, Threats, and Distractions, Consideration 7.4
pages.keyFinding: CAST recommends options that reduce distracting or threatening conditions and recognizes individual differences. Routines, transition cues, adjustable visual stimulation and adjustable activity pace can support participation.
pages.application: Let tutors control what appears to students, announce activity changes, and avoid decorative motion or automatically revealed competing panels during an exercise.

pages.title: Vary and Honor Methods for Response, Navigation, and Movement, Consideration 4.1
pages.keyFinding: Learners differ in how they respond and navigate. Flexible timing, motor demands, selection methods and support for hand, voice, switch, joystick or keyboard input reduce barriers.
pages.application: Offer direct tap/click actions as well as optional movement gestures; do not make speed, precise dragging, or keyboard modifiers prerequisites for instructional participation.

pages.title: Support Opportunities to Customize the Display, Consideration 1.1
pages.keyFinding: Digital presentation can support individual changes to typography, spacing, contrast, imagery, color, sound, timing and layout. Digital content is not inherently accessible merely because it can be displayed on screen.
pages.application: Allow useful scaling, simplified student layouts and restrained appearance preferences; retain semantic text and clear controls instead of relying exclusively on fixed image labels.

pages.title: Enhance Capacity for Monitoring Progress, Consideration 6.4
pages.keyFinding: CAST calls for feedback connected to learning goals that is timely, informative, accessible and customizable. Formative feedback should help learners monitor progress and guide later practice.
pages.application: Distinguish operational feedback such as picture added from learning feedback such as sounds counted; show understandable progress for the current activity without competitive visual clutter.

pages.title: Understanding Headings and Labels
pages.keyFinding: Accurate headings and labels help people anticipate content, find components and understand structure. Short labels can suffice, but an icon's meaning depends on its context and common understanding.
pages.application: Name sections Materials, Games and Video explicitly; keep Add face, Show student and Crop labels distinct rather than presenting an unlabeled chevron or ambiguous icon alone.

pages.title: Understanding Non-text Contrast
pages.keyFinding: Meaningful control boundaries, state indicators and graphics generally require 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. Thin anti-aliased lines can be difficult even when nominal color values pass.
pages.application: Check tab selection, focus outlines, disclosure chevrons, drop targets and disabled-state distinctions; pale dividers alone should not carry the sidebar's structure or affordances.

pages.title: Toolbar Example
pages.keyFinding: The example remembers the most recently focused toolbar control and separates directional navigation from activation. Its demonstration deliberately combines widget types that would not necessarily belong together in a real design.
pages.application: Keep the board tool rail small and coherent, preserve keyboard return position, and use hover labels that also appear on focus and can be dismissed.
